expectedText:
INTERSTATE COMPACT ON THE PLACEMENT OF CHILDREN (ICPC) — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Riley Morgan Lee · April 3, 2016

DECLARATION OF PURPOSE — INTERSTATE COMPACT ON PLACEMENT OF CHILDREN INFORMATION SHEET
This Interstate Compact on Placement of Children (ICPC) Information Sheet describes California's adoption, by California Family Code § 7900, of the multistate compact set out in full at Family Code § 7901, which governs the interstate placement of a child — here, Riley Morgan Lee, born April 3, 2016 — for foster care or as a preliminary to a possible adoption, where the placement involves California and Nevada. Sacramento County Department of Child, Family and Adult Services is identified, for reference, as the person or agency proposing or arranging Riley Morgan Lee's placement.

The ICPC is not itself a permit, license, or court order, and this information sheet does not itself place Riley Morgan Lee anywhere, does not obtain or record any state's approval of a proposed placement, and does not determine whether the compact applies to, excludes, or otherwise governs any specific proposed movement of Riley Morgan Lee across state lines. This document's companion clauses describe the compact's own stated purpose, its definition of a covered "placement" and a statutory exclusion from that definition, its pre-placement notice requirement, its continuing-jurisdiction rule, and California's own statutory designation of the state agency that administers compact notices on California's behalf.

THE COMPACT'S OWN STATEMENT OF PURPOSE AND POLICY
Article 1 of the compact text enacted at California Family Code § 7901 states its own purpose and policy in the compact's own words: "It is the purpose and policy of the party states to cooperate with each other in the interstate placement of children to the end that:" a receiving state's authorities may fully evaluate a proposed placement, a sending state's authorities may obtain complete information before making it, and appropriate jurisdictional arrangements for the child's care are promoted. As Article 1(b) states it, the purpose extends to ensuring "the appropriate authorities in a state where a child is to be placed may have full opportunity to ascertain the circumstances of the proposed placement, thereby promoting full compliance with applicable requirements for the protection of the child." Article 1(d) further states that "appropriate jurisdictional arrangements for the care of children will be promoted."

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "It is the purpose and policy of the party states to cooperate with each other in the interstate placement of children to the end that:"
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 7901, Interstate Compact on the Placement of Children, Art. 1 (California Legislative Information text), Fam. C. § 7901, Art. 1 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=7901.)
  "The appropriate authorities in a state where a child is to be placed may have full opportunity to ascertain the circumstances of the proposed placement, thereby promoting full compliance with applicable requirements for the protection of the child."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 7901, Interstate Compact on the Placement of Children, Art. 1(b) (California Legislative Information text), Fam. C. § 7901, Art. 1(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=7901.)
  "Appropriate jurisdictional arrangements for the care of children will be promoted."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 7901, Interstate Compact on the Placement of Children, Art. 1(d) (California Legislative Information text), Fam. C. § 7901, Art. 1(d) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=7901.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of the compact's own stated purpose as enacted into California law — not a claim about which state's law governs a specific proposed placement, and not a claim that any specific placement of the child named in this document's companion clauses furthers, or fails to further, that purpose. All three citations in this clause are quotations from Article 1 of the single compact text codified at Family Code § 7901, and are not independent of one another. This clause does not quote Article 1(a) or 1(c), which state two further purposes — maximizing a placed child's opportunity for a suitable environment, and letting the sending state's authorities gather complete information before placement — not independently verified beyond the text of Article 1 itself, of which they are also a part. This document is informational only: it does not itself determine that any specific placement of the child named in this document's companion clauses is, or is not, consistent with the compact's stated purpose.

WHAT COUNTS AS A COVERED "PLACEMENT," AND A STATUTORY EXCLUSION FOR CERTAIN RELATIVES
The compact does not apply to every movement of a child across state lines; it applies only to what the compact itself defines as a "placement," and it then expressly excludes certain placements even within that definition. Article 2(d) of the compact text enacted at Family Code § 7901 defines "placement" to mean "the arrangement for the care of a child in a family free or boarding home or in a child-caring agency or institution, but does not include any institution caring for persons with developmental disabilities or mental health disorders or any institution primarily educational in character, and any hospital or other medical facility." Separately, Article 8 of that same compact text states that "this compact shall not apply to: (a) The sending or bringing of a child into a receiving state by the child's parent, stepparent, grandparent, adult brother or sister, adult uncle or aunt, or the child's guardian and leaving the child with any such relative or nonagency guardian in the receiving state."

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "“Placement” means the arrangement for the care of a child in a family free or boarding home or in a child-caring agency or institution, but does not include any institution caring for persons with developmental disabilities or mental health disorders or any institution primarily educational in character, and any hospital or other medical facility."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 7901, Interstate Compact on the Placement of Children, Art. 2(d) (California Legislative Information text), Fam. C. § 7901, Art. 2(d) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=7901.)
  "This compact shall not apply to: (a) The sending or bringing of a child into a receiving state by the child’s parent, stepparent, grandparent, adult brother or sister, adult uncle or aunt, or the child’s guardian and leaving the child with any such relative or nonagency guardian in the receiving state."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 7901, Interstate Compact on the Placement of Children, Art. 8(a) (California Legislative Information text), Fam. C. § 7901, Art. 8(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=7901.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of the compact's own definition of a covered "placement" and of a statutory exclusion for certain relative placements — not a claim about which state's law governs a specific proposed movement of a child across state lines, and not a claim that the movement of the child named in this document's companion clauses is, or is not, excluded under Article 8. Both citations in this clause are Articles of the single compact text codified at Family Code § 7901, and are not independent of one another. Article 8 also excludes, at Article 8(b), a placement made pursuant to a different interstate compact or agreement between the same two states that has the force of law; that separate exclusion is not detailed or quoted in this clause. This clause does not detail Article 2's other three definitions — "child," "sending agency," and "receiving state" — beyond what this document's companion clauses separately quote. This document is informational only: it does not itself determine whether the compact's placement definition, or the Article 8 relative exclusion, applies to any specific proposed movement of the child named in this document's companion clauses; that determination depends on the specific facts, including the identity and relationship of the person sending or bringing the child.

THE PRE-PLACEMENT NOTICE REQUIREMENT BEFORE A CHILD MAY BE SENT INTO ANOTHER STATE
Before a covered placement can lawfully proceed, the sending agency must give the receiving state written notice and may not act until that state responds. Article 3(a) of the compact text enacted at Family Code § 7901 provides that "a sending agency shall not send, bring, or cause to be sent or brought into any other party state any child for placement in foster care or as a preliminary to a possible adoption unless the sending agency complies with each and every requirement set forth in this article and with the applicable laws of the receiving state governing the placement of children therein." Article 3(b) requires that, before doing so, the sending agency "shall furnish the appropriate public authorities in the receiving state written notice of the intention to send, bring, or place the child in the receiving state," containing the child's name, date, and place of birth; the identity and address of the parents or legal guardian; the identity of the person, agency, or institution to whom the child is to be sent; and a statement of the reasons for the proposed placement and the authority for it. Article 3(d) then makes the receiving state's approval a precondition to the placement itself: "the child shall not be sent, brought, or caused to be sent or brought into the receiving state until the appropriate public authorities in the receiving state notify the sending agency, in writing, to the effect that the proposed placement does not appear to be contrary to the interest of the child."

  — Cal. Fam. Code § 7901, Interstate Compact on the Placement of Children, Art. 3(a) (California Legislative Information text), Fam. C. § 7901, Art. 3(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=7901.)
  "Before sending, bringing, or causing any child to be sent or brought into a receiving state for placement in foster care or as a preliminary to a possible adoption, the sending agency shall furnish the appropriate public authorities in the receiving state written notice of the intention to send, bring, or place the child in the receiving state."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 7901, Interstate Compact on the Placement of Children, Art. 3(b) (California Legislative Information text), Fam. C. § 7901, Art. 3(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=7901.)

All three citations in this clause are Articles of the single compact text codified at Family Code § 7901, and are not independent of one another. This clause does not detail Article 3(c)'s separate provision letting the receiving state request additional supporting information from the sending agency, and it does not detail the penalty Article 4 imposes for a placement made in violation of Article 3, which this document does not otherwise cover. A separate California statute, Family Code § 7903, designates the specific California agency that receives and acts on Article 3 notices on this state's behalf; that designation is addressed in this document's companion clause and is not restated here. This document is informational only: it does not itself furnish, receive, or act on any Article 3 notice, and it does not determine that any specific proposed placement of the child named in this document's companion clauses does, or does not, appear contrary to that child's interest.

THE SENDING AGENCY'S CONTINUING JURISDICTION OVER A CHILD PLACED OUT OF STATE
Placing a child in another state under the compact does not transfer legal jurisdiction over that child to the receiving state. Article 5(a) of the compact text enacted at Family Code § 7901 provides that "the sending agency shall retain jurisdiction over the child sufficient to determine all matters in relation to the custody, supervision, care, treatment, and disposition of the child that it would have had if the child had remained in the sending agency's state, until the child is adopted, reaches majority, becomes self-supporting, or is discharged with the concurrence of the appropriate authority in the receiving state." That retained jurisdiction "shall also include the power to effect or cause the return of the child or the child's transfer to another location and custody pursuant to law," and the sending agency "shall continue to have financial responsibility for support and maintenance of the child during the period of the placement." Article 5(a) also preserves the receiving state's own separate authority over conduct occurring there: "nothing contained herein shall defeat a claim of jurisdiction by a receiving state sufficient to deal with an act of delinquency or crime committed therein."

  — Cal. Fam. Code § 7901, Interstate Compact on the Placement of Children, Art. 5(a) (California Legislative Information text), Fam. C. § 7901, Art. 5(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=7901.)
  "Nothing contained herein shall defeat a claim of jurisdiction by a receiving state sufficient to deal with an act of delinquency or crime committed therein."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 7901, Interstate Compact on the Placement of Children, Art. 5(a) (California Legislative Information text), Fam. C. § 7901, Art. 5(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=7901.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of the compact's continuing-jurisdiction rule for a sending agency — not a claim about which state's law governs a specific placement, and not a claim that any sending agency described in this document's companion clauses retains, or has been relieved of, jurisdiction over the child named there in any specific case. This clause quotes only Article 5(a) of the single compact text codified at Family Code § 7901; it does not detail Article 5(b), which lets a public sending agency contract with a receiving-state agency to perform services as the sending agency's agent, or Article 5(c), which addresses a private charitable agency's role in the receiving state, neither of which is independently verified beyond the text of Article 5 itself. A separate California statute, Family Code § 7902, addresses how financial responsibility questions under Article 5 are resolved when a placement partially or completely defaults; that statute is not detailed in this clause. This document is informational only: it does not itself determine, retain, or relieve any jurisdiction over the child named in this document's companion clauses, and it does not determine when that child has been adopted, reached majority, become self-supporting, or been discharged for purposes of Article 5.

THE CALIFORNIA AGENCY DESIGNATED TO RECEIVE AND ACT ON COMPACT NOTICES
Separate from the compact text itself, California has enacted its own statute identifying which California agency the compact's Article 3 notice provisions refer to. Family Code § 7903 provides in full: "The phrase ‘appropriate public authorities’ as used in Article 3 of the Interstate Compact on the Placement of Children means, with reference to this state, the State Department of Social Services, and that department shall receive and act with reference to notices required by Article 3 of the compact." A companion statute, Family Code § 7904, makes the same designation for a related compact term: "The phrase ‘appropriate authority in receiving state’ as used in paragraph (a) of Article 5 of the Interstate Compact on the Placement of Children, with reference to this state, means the State Department of Social Services."

Family Code § 7903 and § 7904 are two separate, independently numbered statutory sections, cited here as two independent sources; neither is a subsection of the other or of Family Code § 7901, the section codifying the compact text itself. This clause does not detail Family Code § 7905, which separately empowers California officers and agencies to enter into Article 5(b) service agreements with other party states, subject to Controller or local fiscal officer approval for any agreement carrying a financial commitment, or Family Code § 7902's rule on resolving financial-responsibility defaults; neither is independently verified beyond what this clause states. This document is informational only: it does not itself constitute, request, or record any notice, application, or approval addressed to the State Department of Social Services, and it does not determine that department's disposition of any specific proposed placement of the child named in this document's companion clauses.

citations.quote: The phrase “appropriate public authorities” as used in Article 3 of the Interstate Compact on the Placement of Children means, with reference to this state, the State Department of Social Services, and that department shall receive and act with reference to notices required by Article 3 of the compact.

expectedJSON.gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of which California agency the compact's Article 3 and Article 5(a) terms refer to as enacted into California law — not a claim about which agency, if any, administers the compact in a different party state, and not a claim about how the State Department of Social Services in fact carries out that role in practice, day to day, beyond what these two statutes themselves state. Family Code § 7903 and § 7904 are two separate, independently numbered statutory sections, cited here as two independent sources; neither is a subsection of the other or of Family Code § 7901, the section codifying the compact text itself. This clause does not detail Family Code § 7905, which separately empowers California officers and agencies to enter into Article 5(b) service agreements with other party states, subject to Controller or local fiscal officer approval for any agreement carrying a financial commitment, or Family Code § 7902's rule on resolving financial-responsibility defaults; neither is independently verified beyond what this clause states. This document is informational only: it does not itself constitute, request, or record any notice, application, or approval addressed to the State Department of Social Services, and it does not determine that department's disposition of any specific proposed placement of the child named in this document's companion clauses.
